title: Reckoning the Allowance Still Owed for Benefit Periods Already Gone
content:
This is the basis on which the allowance still owed to a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card for benefit periods that have already gone by is reckoned.

**The amount.** The allowance still owed is what the schedule owed for the benefit periods already gone, held at the ceiling on the benefit year, less what has already been made available, never less than nothing and rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier step.

**What the schedule owed.** What the schedule owed is the share of the first benefit period the allowance is owed for, together with the whole allowance of each benefit period from that one up to the last that has fallen due. The share of that first period is the allowance a benefit period carries divided by the months in a benefit period and multiplied by the months of that first period the allowance is owed for. The whole allowance of the periods after it is the allowance a benefit period carries multiplied by the number of benefit periods by which the last that has fallen due stands beyond the first.

**The allowance a benefit period carries.** The allowance a benefit period carries is the quarterly allowance the member's medical plan tier carries where that is larger than the card's own, and the card's own quarterly allowance otherwise.

**The months in a benefit period.** A benefit period runs 3 months where the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year, 12 months where it is made available once a year, and 1 month in every other case.

**Where it is placed.** The allowance still owed is placed in the benefit period in which it is made available, because it makes good several benefit periods at once and belongs to none of them alone.

**The standing values.** The benefit periods that have passed are taken to be counted as the whole months of the benefit year gone by. The first benefit period the allowance is owed for is taken to be the benefit period the programme opened in. The months of that first period the allowance is owed for are taken as the whole of a benefit period. The last benefit period that has fallen due is taken to be the period before the current one. What has already been made available is taken as nothing. The ceiling on the benefit year is taken as the allowance a benefit period carries.

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** Take a card whose tier carries a quarterly allowance of 90.00 USD, held alongside a medical plan tier carrying 60.00 USD, whose allowance is loaded on calendar quarters, and where 7 whole months of the benefit year have gone by. The allowance a benefit period carries is 90.00 USD, the card's own being the larger. A benefit period runs 3 months. The benefit periods that have passed are counted as the whole months of the benefit year gone by, so 7 have passed and the current period is the 7th. The first period the allowance is owed for is the one the programme opened in, say the 4th, and the months of it owed are the whole of a benefit period, 3. The last period that has fallen due is the 6th. The share of the first period is 90.00 USD divided by 3 and multiplied by 3, that is 90.00 USD; the periods beyond it number 2, carrying 180.00 USD; so the schedule owed 270.00 USD. The ceiling on the benefit year is 90.00 USD, so the figure is held at 90.00 USD. Nothing has already been made available, so the allowance still owed is 90.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end.
